To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The dwarf shrubs dominating the plant communities, Vaccinium myltillus and V. vltis-idaea took up little of added NH4+ or NO3- independent of the chemical forms, and their growth was not affected by the treatments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of nitrogen (N) addition to boreal forest undergrowth.
how N deposition affects the boreal forest undergrowth and the natural enemies of its dominant species.
the effects of N on the vegetation and natural enemies in a boreal forest ecosystem in Northern Sweden.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N load a boreal ecosystem can sustain without substantial negative effects depends on the relative contribution of the two N forms in the deposition.
the N form does matter for the response of boreal forest undergrowth.
the responses of plants to the N additions in this study are not related to the chemical form of N.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N deposition in the studied area is too low for the plant species to respond to the addition.
NH4+ is the most critical N form in terms of effects on the vegetation.
NH4+ is a more potent driver for changes in the boreal understorey plant community and the associated plant pathogenic fungi than NO3-.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N load a boreal forest can sustain without substantial change to the vegetation should be set considering the specific vegetation response to the predominant N forms in deposition.
the relative contribution of the N forms to the total deposition should be considered when assessing the effects of N deposition on the vegetation and its natural enemies.
the relative importance of the two N forms for plant and fungi growth is not the same.
